meta.method: WebSearch and WebFetch. Where a page returned 403/404 to WebFetch, the only evidence was the search engine's summary of it, and the entry says so ('search summary'). No quotation here is longer than what the fetch or summary returned. 'Supports' fields say only what the named source was seen to say.

low.activityClaim: Watch animated features or shorts at a free Yale screening (Films at the Whitney, Yale Film Archive) or study scenes frame by frame at home.
low.activitySupports: Page says 'All events are free and open to all'; venue 320 York St.; screenings mostly at 7:00 or 7:30 pm. It listed NAUSICAÄ OF THE VALLEY OF THE WIND (1984) in 35mm for 8 October 2026, so animation is programmed at least sometimes. No standing animation strand.
low.actorUseClaim: Studying animation in reverse shows an actor how a clear thought precedes and shapes a gesture, since animators are trained in acting theory (Hooks).
low.actorUseSupports: Routledge page (5th edition, 2023, Ed Hooks) says the book 'applies classical acting theory – from Aristotle to Stanislavsky and beyond – to animation' and explains 'the connections between thinking, emotion and physical action'. A search summary says the 4th edition (2017) has a chapter titled 'Thinking tends to lead to conclusions, and emotion tends to lead to action'. Nothing says actors learn from watching animation.
low.how: Inference: the pedagogy runs from acting to animators. Watching animation as an actor relies on reversing it.
low.uncertainty: The thought-before-action principle is documented for animators, not as an actor exercise. The cited URL is the 5th edition (2023), not an earlier one.

low.activityClaim: Visit the free Yale School of Architecture Gallery or the Yale Center for British Art to study how interiors are composed, then rewatch a film scene and list what the set says about who lives there.
low.activitySupports: YCBA: 'Admission to the Yale Center for British Art is free.' Open Tue 10–5, Wed 10–7, Thu–Sat 10–5, Sun 11–5; closed Mondays and listed holidays. The cited /admission-and-hours URL returned 403. A search summary of catalog.yale.edu gives the Architecture Gallery as 2nd floor of Paul Rudolph Hall, 180 York St, open Mon–Fri 9–5 and Sat 10–5, with 'The public is welcome at all events.'
low.actorUseClaim: Reading the designed environment as given circumstances, i.e. Hagen's 'where' and Shurtleff's 'Place' guidepost.
low.actorUseSupports: Shurtleff's Guidepost 10 Place: 'Where are you? What's around you? ... What's your emotional connection to this place?' The BYU page on Hagen's basic object exercise lists her questions, including 'Where am I? What surrounds me?'. Both ask the actor to make place specific. Neither mentions studying designed sets or paintings.
low.how: Analogy: practising reading a designed space for character information, which these tools ask the actor to imagine.
low.uncertainty: Both acting tools are verified. That studying art direction trains them is inference. The originally cited Goodreads page is only a book listing.

low.activityClaim: Watch a film at a free Yale screening for colour mood, or try a CCAM editing/post workshop.
low.activitySupports: Films at the Whitney is free and open to all. The CCAM sponsored-courses page lists credit courses (e.g. 'Cinematography: History, Theory, Practice', Tuesdays 2:30–6:30pm), not drop-in workshops. A search summary says C-CAMP workshops cover motion capture, projection mapping, mixed reality, cinematography and video editing, with 'no prior experience necessary'. No grading-specific workshop found. CCAM uses DaVinci Resolve Studio, which does colour grading (creativecow search result).
low.actorUseClaim: Noticing how colour carries a scene's mood feeds Michael Chekhov's 'atmosphere' work.
low.actorUseSupports: A search summary confirms Chekhov's To the Actor has a chapter 'The Atmosphere and Individual Feelings'. The originally cited Wikipedia page on Michael Chekhov does NOT mention atmosphere (checked). A search summary of the Lecoq school's first-year page lists 'dynamic study of nature (elements and materials, colours and lights...)', and the NSW education overview says the first year explores 'sound and colour'.
low.how: Analogy: colour as a carrier of mood connects to Chekhov's atmosphere and Lecoq's colour work. Neither concerns film grading.
low.uncertainty: The original citation (Chekhov Wikipedia) does not support the atmosphere claim and should be replaced. Unverified that a grading workshop exists at Yale.

low.activityClaim: Watch a free Films at the Whitney screening and write a 500-word review focusing on one performance.
low.activitySupports: Free and open to all; evening screenings (typically 7:00/7:30 pm) at 320 York St.
low.actorUseClaim: Articulating why a performance works trains the analytical half of the craft.
low.actorUseSupports: The Yale acting plan of study lists 'DRAM 4b - Critical Response Process®' in Year One, plus Text Analysis I and II. A search summary describes Liz Lerman's Critical Response Process (1990) as 'a method for giving and getting feedback on creative work in progress' in four steps. So structured response to others' work is part of the Yale actor's training. A written review of a finished film is a different form.
low.how: Analogy: verbalised critique of performance resembles the CRP and text-analysis work in the Yale curriculum.
low.uncertainty: No source says writing criticism improves acting. CRP is a better curricular anchor than the original null source, but it is feedback on work in progress, not reviewing.

low.activityClaim: Attend free screenings at NHdocs, held at the New Haven Free Public Library and Yale venues.
low.activitySupports: NHdocs NO LONGER RUNS. The festival's own site is titled 'NHdocs: the New Haven Documentary Film Festival (2014 to 2023)'. Moviejawn (June 2025) says the festival 'ended in 2023'. Members of the NHdocs team started the Lighthouse Lens Film Festival (5–8 June 2025, at The Cannon and the New Haven Arts Council's Sandbox; ticketed, price not stated). Wikipedia still describes NHdocs as free, at the Whitney Humanities Center, NHFPL and Cafe Nine, but that is historical.
low.actorUseClaim: Documentaries offer real people's speech and behaviour as raw material for observation (Lecoq, Stanislavski-based training).
low.actorUseSupports: 'The first year is devoted to observation of the world and of the movements in it...' Lecoq's observation is of life, not of film.
low.how: Analogy: filmed real behaviour as a substitute for live observation.
low.uncertainty: The activity as written is unavailable. Rewrite it around Films at the Whitney documentaries or Lighthouse Lens, if it recurs; no 2026 edition was confirmed.

low.activityClaim: Attend 'Treasures from the Yale Film Archive', a free year-round series of classic 35mm films with introductions and notes.
low.activitySupports: 'These screenings are always free and open to the public.' Films in 35mm. Upcoming dates were Thu 29 Oct 2026 7pm, Thu 5 Nov 7pm and Fri 13 Nov 7pm, at Humanities Quadrangle Lower Level, 320 York St. Runtimes listed 69–88 min. There are introductions and linked film notes.
low.actorUseClaim: Studying performance styles across eras shows how acting conventions change; useful for period pieces.
low.actorUseSupports: The Yale plan includes 'DRAM 873a/b - Global Theater and Performance: A Theater History Survey'. That is theatre history, not film. No source ties film-history viewing to actor development.
low.how: Analogy from theatre-history study to film-history viewing.
low.uncertainty: Activity well verified; actor-use unsupported by any pedagogy text found.

low.activityClaim: Attend a free Yale Film Archive screening and read about the Archive's preservation projects (7,000+ 35mm/16mm titles; FIAF associate).
low.activitySupports: The About page says 'more than 8,000 film elements' and 'more than 50,000 assets in our video collection', and calls the archive 'A Member of the International Federation of Film Archives (FIAF)'. So '7,000+ titles' and 'FIAF associate' do not match the current page. It has a conservation suite with cold storage. A 'Preserved Films' page exists.
low.actorUseClaim: Archival prints are a primary source for how people moved and spoke in earlier decades.
low.actorUseSupports: No source found.
low.how: Inference: period behaviour research.
low.uncertainty: Correct the figures to '8,000+ film elements' and 'FIAF member'. The actor-use claim is unsourced.

low.activityClaim: Record ordinary actions on a phone and match them to a muted film clip.
low.activitySupports: Home practice; no venue needed. No New Haven Foley resource found.
low.actorUseClaim: Foley's exact re-creation of how an action sounds is close to Hagen's object exercises.
low.actorUseSupports: BYU teaching page: the basic object exercise has students perform 'a 2-minute slice of their life', guided by nine questions. A search summary says Hagen's object exercises re-create behaviour, e.g. getting a cup of coffee. Nothing about sound.
low.how: Analogy: attention to the specific physical behaviour of everyday actions.
low.uncertainty: Pure analogy. The Backstage guide originally cited returned 403.

low.activityClaim: At a Yale Rep or Cabaret performance, watch where actors stand to find light; or note window light on faces in YUAG portraits.
low.activitySupports: YUAG: 'The Gallery is free and open to the public.' Tue–Fri 10–5, Thu (Sept–June) to 8pm, Sat–Sun 11–5; closed Mondays. Yale Cabaret student single ticket $16 (yalecabaret.org/visit-us). Yale Rep offers 'substantially discounted tickets' for students (FAQ; price not stated).
low.actorUseClaim: 'Finding your light' and hitting marks are working skills; Caine's Acting in Film covers screen technical awareness.
low.actorUseSupports: A search summary describes Caine's book (from a 1987 BBC workshop; Applause, 1990) as covering hitting marks, continuity and not blinking in close-up. Another summary says it 'addresses voice, sound, lighting, and movement', but no lighting passage was seen. A Backstage article titled 'The Must-Know Trick for Finding Your Light Onstage' exists (403; search summary: 'it is the actor's responsibility to perform where the lights are shining'). That is trade journalism, not pedagogy.
low.how: Practical skill: knowing where light falls lets the actor be seen. Watching from the audience is an indirect way to learn it.
low.uncertainty: Caine's treatment of lighting is unverified. 'Find your light' is industry common knowledge with only trade-press sourcing here.

low.activityClaim: Walk New Haven (East Rock, the Green, Wooster Square) photographing places where a scene from a current play could happen.
low.activitySupports: A search summary of the city facility page (403 to fetch) and Wikipedia: East Rock Park is 427 acres, closed 'sunset to sunrise', with over 10 miles of trails. The summit is reachable on foot or by bicycle Mon–Sat and by car on Sundays (seasonal road hours).
low.actorUseClaim: Making the place of a scene specific (Shurtleff's 'Place'; Hagen's 'where').
low.actorUseSupports: Shurtleff Place: 'Where are you? What's around you? Are you indoors; outdoors...'. Hagen's questions include 'Where am I? What surrounds me?'. A search summary says 'What surrounds me?' covers 'the immediate landscape, the weather, the condition of the place, and the nature of the objects in it'.
low.how: Gathering concrete real places to answer Place / Where questions.
low.uncertainty: The acting tools are verified. That location-hunting is used to feed them is plausible but undocumented, so it remains an analogy.

low.activityClaim: Build a cardboard model box of a play's set at a desk, or use the free Ives Squared makerspace at the New Haven Free Public Library.
low.activitySupports: Ives Squared (Ives Main Library, 133 Elm St) includes 'the Tinker Lab, a makerspace'. Equipment includes laser cutters, 3D printers, CNC routers, Cricut, sewing machines. 'Certification is required to use our laser cutter, 3D printers, and CNC routing machine': training videos, then a scheduled certification test. Ives Squared hours: Mon–Thu 10–7:30, Fri–Sat 10–4:30. Cost and card requirement were not stated on the fetched pages; a search summary says the space is open to anyone with a library card and classes are free.
low.actorUseClaim: Hands-on craft is associated with better mood and life satisfaction (Frontiers in Public Health 2024, 7,182 adults); also lets the actor plan blocking in the set's space.
low.actorUseSupports: Keyes et al., 'Creating arts and crafting positively predicts subjective wellbeing': 7,182 adults in England, secondary analysis of the Taking Part Survey 2019–20. Crafting 'significantly predicted increased life satisfaction, a sense that life is worthwhile and happiness', but did not significantly reduce anxiety or loneliness. Nothing about blocking.
low.how: Association (cross-sectional) between crafting and wellbeing. The blocking use is unsourced.
low.uncertainty: The wellbeing claim as worded matches the source, but it is an association, not a measured recovery effect. Wording should be 'happiness' rather than 'mood', and should note no effect on anxiety. The blocking claim has no source.

low.activityClaim: Build a playlist for a character and listen to it during preparation.
low.activitySupports: Home activity, no venue.
low.actorUseClaim: Musical impulse shapes inner state, as in Stanislavski's tempo-rhythm; music listening also aids stress recovery.
low.actorUseSupports: Building a Character has chapters 11 'Tempo-Rhythm in Movement' and 12 'Speech Tempo-Rhythm' (Wikipedia list); playlists are not mentioned. The PLOS ONE 2022 meta-analysis (Adiasto et al., 14 studies, N=706) found NO significant benefit of music listening for stress recovery: g=0.15, 95% CI [-0.21, 0.52], p=0.374, and 'no definite conclusions may currently be drawn'. A Backstage article 'Your Character's Soundtrack' exists (403; search summary describes playlists as a tool actors use). That is trade press.
low.how: Analogy to tempo-rhythm. The recovery claim is contradicted by its own cited source.
low.uncertainty: Remove or reword the recovery claim. If a recovery source is wanted, de Witte et al. 2020 (Health Psychology Review, 104 RCTs) found music interventions reduced stress (d=.380 physiological, .545 psychological), but those were interventions, not self-chosen playlists.

low.activityClaim: Read about and watch behind-the-scenes material on practical effects; or try simple builds at the library makerspace.
low.activitySupports: Tinker Lab exists with laser cutter, 3D printers, CNC and sewing machines. Certification is required for the laser cutter, 3D printers and CNC.
low.actorUseClaim: Hagen's endowment exercise (giving an object qualities it lacks) is the acting tool for fake blood, breakaway glass etc.
low.actorUseSupports: Fetch returned 403. A search summary of Hagen sources: endowment 'gives a characteristic or quality to something that it doesn't actually have... (like making a cup of cold water seem like hot tea)', and helps actors 'endow props with qualities that they cannot safely have on stage'.
low.how: Direct application of endowment to props whose real qualities differ from the fiction.
low.uncertainty: Endowment for unsafe props is close to what the sources say. That studying effects builds it is an inference. Fake blood and breakaway glass are not named in any source seen.

low.activityClaim: Help produce a Yale Cabaret show or a classmate's reading: book a room, schedule rehearsals, print programmes.
low.activitySupports: 'The Yale Cabaret is an independent, student-run theater company in residence at David Geffen School of Drama', 'strictly extracurricular', including 'self-scripted material, company-devised original work'. Cabaret site: 'Entirely student-run, the Cabaret reinvents itself each season under new leadership', at 217 Park Street. A search summary (drama.yale.edu) says it is where students move out of their discipline: 'actors direct, managers act'.
low.actorUseClaim: Yale's acting training progresses toward self-generated performance, which requires producing one's own work.
low.actorUseSupports: The plan includes 'development of self-generated performance material' and 'DRAM 363a - You Are the Creator'. A search summary of the Yale bulletin says it lets actors 'explore, develop, and create their own individual performance pieces'.
low.how: Producing logistics are what self-generated work requires; the Cabaret is the documented outlet.
low.uncertainty: Self-generated work and Cabaret cross-discipline roles are verified. That an acting student takes a producing role specifically is plausible but not documented.

low.activityClaim: Visit the free Yale School of Architecture Gallery (Rudolph Hall) and see student design work; sketch a set for a scene.
low.activitySupports: The fetched exhibitions page names it 'Yale Architecture Gallery', 2nd floor, weekdays 9–5 and Saturdays 10–5. It gave the address as 190 York Street, but other sources (catalog.yale.edu search summary, NHBA) give Rudolph Hall as 180 York Street. A search summary of catalog.yale.edu: the school shows 'an annual exhibition of student work', 'The public is welcome at all events'. Admission not stated on the fetched page.
low.actorUseClaim: Viewpoints treats architecture and topography as performance material.
low.actorUseSupports: Bogart's spatial viewpoints: Architecture, Spatial Relationship, Topography, Shape, Gesture. Overlie originated the Six Viewpoints. Bogart & Landau, The Viewpoints Book (2005).
low.how: Analogy: studying designed space as material, as Viewpoints Architecture asks the actor to respond to the real space.
low.uncertainty: Viewpoints responds to the room the actor is in, not to drawings or set designs. The gallery's name varies by source, and its address on the fetched page (190) conflicts with 180 York St.

low.activityClaim: Film the same short action three times on a phone and check whether props, hands and lines match between takes.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: Matching action and business across takes is a core screen skill; the Yale plan includes On-Camera Acting Technique.
low.actorUseSupports: The blog page reproduces excerpts of Caine's Acting in Film, including a 'miniature golf' passage on matching physical actions across long, medium and close-up shots (fetch summary). A search summary of the book: 'A keen awareness of picture continuity is essential...'. The Yale plan lists 'DRAM 463a - On-Camera Acting Technique' and says students learn 'to work on camera and in front of a microphone'. Wikipedia (search summary): a script supervisor checks 'that the actions and eye-lines of the actors match'.
low.how: Direct: the actor's own continuity is a screen-acting skill named in Caine.
low.uncertainty: Caine's continuity material is seen through a blog excerpt and summaries, not the book itself. The self-filming drill is not itself documented.

low.activityClaim: Look at furnished period rooms and interiors depicted at the Yale Center for British Art, listing what each object says about its owner.
low.activitySupports: Free admission; open Tue–Sun, closed Mondays. Whether 'furnished period rooms' (as opposed to painted interiors) are on display was not checked.
low.actorUseClaim: An actor's relationship to the objects in a room (Hagen's endowment) makes a set feel lived in.
low.actorUseSupports: Hagen's questions include 'What surrounds me?'. A search summary says this question covers 'the condition of the place, and the nature of the objects in it'. Endowment gives objects qualities they lack (search summary).
low.how: Analogy: reading objects for owner and history, as Hagen asks the actor to know the objects around them.
low.uncertainty: Tool verified; transfer from looking at paintings is inference. YCBA's collection is chiefly paintings, so 'depicted' interiors is the accurate wording.

low.activityClaim: Watch a full season of a TV drama and chart how each character changes episode to episode.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: Series acting requires tracking a character across many episodes.
low.actorUseSupports: No source found.
low.how: Inference.
low.uncertainty: Unsourced. A full season is many hours, not one.

low.activityClaim: Sit in a park or café for 30 minutes with eyes closed and list every sound; or listen to a radio drama.
low.activitySupports: East Rock Park is open sunrise to sunset (search summary of the city page, which returned 403).
low.actorUseClaim: Chekhov's atmosphere work and attentive listening both depend on sensitivity to the sound of a space.
low.actorUseSupports: The NSW Lecoq overview: the first year explores 'the natural elements, animals, words, sound and colour'. Davidson (2023, Theatre, Dance and Performance Training; search summary) argues Meisner Technique and Dalcroze ear training 'promote similar forms of responsive, interpretative, and collaborative listening'. The originally cited Chekhov Wikipedia page does not mention atmosphere.
low.how: Analogy: ambient listening as sensory training, near Lecoq's sound observation.
low.uncertainty: Listening in Meisner means listening to a partner, not to ambient sound. The Chekhov citation should be replaced.

low.activityClaim: Record a monologue on a phone at different distances and levels and listen back.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: Yale trains actors for audio; hearing oneself recorded calibrates microphone technique.
low.actorUseSupports: Verbatim (fetch): students take 'multiple courses in learning to work on camera and in front of a microphone, transferring their acquired skills to the mediums of film and audio recording.' A search summary of SAG-AFTRA self-tape guidance stresses audio quality ('Poor audio quality can be the biggest distraction...').
low.how: Direct practice of a curricular skill (microphone work).
low.uncertainty: Microphone work is in the curriculum. Self-recording as a practice method is plausible but not documented.

low.activityClaim: Storyboard a monologue as six panels in a sketchbook.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: Visualising images behind the text, as Chekhov's technique asks.
low.actorUseSupports: A search summary: To the Actor, Chapter 2 'Imagination and Incorporation of Images'. The originally cited Wikipedia page says only that Chekhov taught 'a physical and imagination-based system'; it does not mention imagined images.
low.how: Analogy: drawing externalises the images Chekhov asks the actor to see inwardly.
low.uncertainty: Drawing is not Chekhov's method. Chapter title confirmed only by search summary.

low.activityClaim: Watch title sequences and note how they set a film's tone.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: Noticing how a film announces its genre may help an actor pitch a performance.
low.actorUseSupports: No source found.
low.how: Inference.
low.uncertainty: No credible link found.

low.activityClaim: Join classmates to pitch and improvise scene ideas.
low.activitySupports: The Cabaret takes 'company-devised original work'. The Carlotta Festival has actors working on new plays by third-year playwrights. The plan of study lists 'DRAM 51b - New Play Lab'.
low.actorUseClaim: Idea-building in a room shares improv's 'yes, and' logic.
low.actorUseSupports: Spolin's games each have 'a focus, a problem to be solved by the players as a group'. 'Yes, and' is not on the page.
low.how: Analogy: group problem-solving.
low.uncertainty: Devising and new-play work are documented at Yale, but not as writers'-room pitching.

low.activityClaim: Read automotive books from NHFPL, watch driving scenes, or observe how people get in and out of cars on New Haven streets.
low.activitySupports: NHFPL main branch is the Ives Memorial Library on the Green; about 485,823 items. Automotive holdings not checked.
low.actorUseClaim: How a person handles a machine reveals status and temperament, like Lecoq's observation of the world and Hagen's object work; driving scenes are a screen skill.
low.actorUseSupports: 'The first year is devoted to observation of the world and of the movements in it'. A search summary of the school page lists 'play and re-play of daily life'. Nothing about cars.
low.how: Analogy: everyday-behaviour observation.
low.uncertainty: No source ties cars to actor training.

low.activityClaim: Study dress and how it shapes posture in portraits at YCBA or YUAG, then people-watch on Chapel Street noting what clothing signals.
low.activitySupports: Both free; YCBA open Tue–Sun; YUAG open Tue–Sun (Thu to 8pm Sept–June); both closed Mondays.
low.actorUseClaim: Brecht's gestus makes social class visible in outward bearing; dress carries it.
low.actorUseSupports: Gestus page: it 'makes visible a character's social relations'; it does not mention clothing. Building a Character, Chapter 2 is 'Dressing a Character', and the article says the volume 'extends to the usage and wearing of costumes, including how the actor wears them and uses them to enrich the character'.
low.how: Stanislavski explicitly ties how clothes are worn to character. Gestus covers social signalling but not dress.
low.uncertainty: Raised from low because Building a Character directly addresses dress and character, but only via a Wikipedia summary. The gestus-to-clothing step is still inference. Overlaps costume_design.

low.activityClaim: Set up and test a phone self-tape rig (light, sound, framing), or take a no-experience-needed CCAM workshop in motion capture, projection mapping or video editing.
low.activitySupports: Event page returned 404 to fetch. A search summary: C-CAMP is 'a daylong event... held early each semester' of workshops in motion capture, projection mapping, video editing and more; 'No prior experience is necessary!'. The original filmnet URL now redirects to film.yale.edu, which returned 404.
low.actorUseClaim: Self-taping is now routine for auditions; LAMDA teaches motion capture for performance.
low.actorUseSupports: SAG-AFTRA runs self-tape pages and trainings (search listing: 'Self-Tape Anatomy', 'Self-Tape & Live Remote Audition Training'). A Backstage piece is titled 'SAG-AFTRA Has Made Self-Taping an Industry Norm'. Its summary recommends front light (ring light or a window behind the camera, filmed during the day) and good audio. LAMDA (search summary): a two-day course combining 'LAMDA's movement and acting techniques' with motion capture, fee £475.
low.how: Direct: self-tape set-up is an audition skill documented by the actors' union.
low.uncertainty: SAG-AFTRA and LAMDA pages could not be fetched (403); evidence is search summaries. C-CAMP dates for the current term not confirmed.

low.activityClaim: Watch an episode of a TV drama and track one character's objective scene by scene.
low.activitySupports: Home activity.
low.actorUseClaim: On-camera work and script analysis over a series arc; screen technique as in Caine.
low.actorUseSupports: Plan includes Text Analysis I/II and On-Camera Acting Technique. No source on TV viewing as training. Caine's book is about film acting technique (search summary).
low.how: Analogy: objective-tracking (text analysis) applied to TV.
low.uncertainty: Unsourced as a practice.

low.activityClaim: Without travelling: listen to speakers from other regions on the free IDEA archive and read travel writing.
low.activitySupports: 'The International Dialects of English Archive was created in 1998' by Paul Meier; free ('Please consider supporting this free research website').
low.actorUseClaim: Knight-Thompson Speechwork's 'Four Ps' start from People, treating accents as they exist in the world.
low.actorUseSupports: 'KTS addresses accents under four headings: People, Posture, Prosody, and Pronunciation'. People is 'an investigation of the world in which an accent is spoken, the societal, historical, and geographical context'. IDEA: Meier 'established IDEA to provide actors the real-life models they need for their characters' accents and dialects.' The Yale plan has Speech and Accents I–III.
low.how: Direct for accent work. The interest-to-activity step (travel replaced by listening) is a substitution.
low.uncertainty: The actor-use claim is now directly sourced from primary pages. What stays weak is that this activity stands in for 'travel'. Overlaps dialect_coaching.

constraints.detail: Films at the Whitney screenings are mostly evening, 7:00 or 7:30 pm; animation is programmed only occasionally (e.g. Nausicaä, 8 Oct 2026).
320 York St (Humanities Quadrangle); free and open to all.
YCBA closed Mondays; Tue 10–5, Wed 10–7, Thu–Sat 10–5, Sun 11–5.
Architecture Gallery open weekdays 9–5 and Saturdays 10–5; not listed as open Sundays.
Payne Whitney Gym membership required; free and auto-activated for current students.
Group fitness classes need a paid Group Fitness Class Pass on top of membership (1-week trial or semester passes; prices not shown).
Standard group fitness classes are 60 minutes.
Classes in morning (about 7–9am) and late-afternoon/evening (about 4:30–7:30pm) slots; the only dance-style class seen was WERQ; schedule begins 31 August, some classes 2–3 weeks later.
Treasures from the Yale Film Archive: specific evenings at 7pm (e.g. Thu 29 Oct, Thu 5 Nov, Fri 13 Nov 2026).
Listed Treasures features run 69–88 minutes.
C-CAMP is a single daylong event held early each semester (search summary).
Films at the Whitney: evening screenings, typically 7:00/7:30 pm.
C-CAMP workshops are a once-a-semester daylong event (search summary).
YCBA and YUAG both closed Mondays; YCBA Tue–Sun, YUAG Tue–Fri 10–5 (Thu to 8pm Sept–June), Sat–Sun 11–5.
Peabody Museum open Tue–Fri 10–5 and Sat–Sun 12–5 (as fetched); closed Mondays. Free admission.
Yale Cabaret student single ticket $16 (DGSD student $10); $2.50 online processing fee.
Yale Rep: 'substantially discounted' student tickets; price not stated.
Yale Rep productions run in fixed windows (e.g. 2–24 Oct 2026; 14 Nov–5 Dec 2026).
Evening screenings, typically 7:00/7:30 pm.
NHdocs ran 2014–2023 and has ended; its successor, Lighthouse Lens, ran 5–8 June 2025 (once a year at most, in summer, outside term).
Lighthouse Lens is ticketed ('tickets are on sale now'); price not stated.
Treasures screenings on set evenings at 7pm (Thu/Fri in the listed run).
Listed features 69–88 minutes, plus introductions.
Same Treasures evening schedule (7pm on set dates).
YSM Lunchtime Chamber Music is on Wednesdays at 12:30 PM in Morse Recital Hall (Sprague Memorial Hall); free, no registration (search summary of YSM ticket pages).
Spolin games have 'a problem to be solved by the players as a group'.
Improvaganza is a single evening event (7pm, start of the year in 2022); a search summary says groups give free shows in the first week of school.
The pillars presuppose scene partners: choreography is 'what goes where, with whom', and consent requires continual check-ins (search summary).
Cabaret student ticket $16; Rep discounted student tickets.
YUAG closed Mondays; Tue–Fri 10–5 (Thu to 8pm Sept–June), Sat–Sun 11–5.
East Rock Park is closed sunset to sunrise (search summary of city page).
Laser cutter, 3D printers and CNC need staff certification (training videos plus a scheduled certification test).
Ives Squared hours Mon–Thu 10am–7:30pm, Fri–Sat 10am–4:30pm; no Sunday hours listed.
Workshops occur at C-CAMP, a daylong event early each semester (search summary); otherwise listed per event.
Motion capture is in CCAM's Leeds Studio (search summary of CCAM Leeds Studio page).
Tinker Lab machine use (laser cutter, 3D printers, CNC) requires certification.
Yale Cabaret, 217 Park St, student-run, new leadership each season.
